justification: OCR extraction fallback (#832 integration, Phase-0 passed 3/3): when a chapter's PDF text layer is garbled, page texts come from the Unlimited-OCR Modal endpoint (pixels, not text layer) and feed the SAME section splitter; everything downstream (diff, review queue, fidelity gates, commit) unchanged. Fail-visible: endpoint unset/unreachable means extraction proceeds on the text layer exactly as today. Deploy source for the Modal service lives in the repo (the panels/structures deploys came from an untracked folder - lesson applied).

pre_impl.existing_data: Phase-0 eval (issue #832) passed all three hard chapters: zero garble on KRG interleave, CoS letter-spaced headers, Woollahra watermark; tables emerge as structured markup. Endpoint deployed and smoke-tested live (200, clean text, auth enforced, 401 without token). Weights pinned to revision 27a5997f in Modal volume unlimited-ocr-weights.
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: The model emits detection tags in the form tag+blocktype+coords - the first normaliser regex left the block-type word behind (caught by test). pdfplumber table extraction reads the garbled text layer, so in OCR mode inline flattened table rows replace it rather than running both.
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: The seam is one helper (_page_text) covering all three existing page-read sites; the splitter, TOC override, diff and queue logic are untouched. Trigger is deterministic: doubled-glyph runs in the raw text layer AND MODAL_OCR_URL set. The AI_EXTRACTION path is unrelated and unchanged.

functions.name: fetch_ocr_page_texts
functions.input: chapter PDF path; MODAL_OCR_URL and MODAL_OCR_TOKEN from env
functions.output: list of normalised per-page texts from the OCR endpoint
functions.if_none: missing env, non-200, junk payload, or any exception returns None with a printed reason - the caller stays on the text layer and the fidelity gates flag the rows as they do today

functions.name: normalise_ocr_page
functions.input: raw model output for one page including detection tags and table markup
functions.output: plain splitter-ready text with tables flattened to pipe-separated rows
functions.if_none: empty or None input returns empty string; no exception paths

functions.name: text_layer_garbled
functions.input: raw pdfplumber page texts for the chapter
functions.output: True when any page carries doubled-glyph runs (the OCR trigger)
functions.if_none: empty or None pages contribute False - a blank text layer alone never triggers OCR

values.value: OCR page texts replacing the garbled text layer for flagged chapters
values.read_at: ChapterExtractor._page_text (line 825) serving ocr_pages when set; the three read sites all route through it
values.if_missing: ocr_pages None means every site reads pdfplumber exactly as before this change

queries: N/A - no database access added; the queue insert path is untouched.

break_it.scenario: The Modal endpoint is down or slow when a garbled chapter extracts.
break_it.what_happens: The chapter would block on OCR or crash the cron mid-run.
break_it.how: fetch_ocr_page_texts catches everything (timeout 1800s) and returns None; extraction proceeds on the text layer and the rows fail fidelity visibly, exactly the pre-change behaviour. Four failure modes pinned by tests.
break_it.repro: Set MODAL_OCR_URL to an unreachable host and extract a garbled chapter - rows enqueue with fidelity failed.

break_it.scenario: OCR mode silently loses table data because pdfplumber table extraction is skipped.
break_it.what_happens: Parking-rate style tables would vanish from review text.
break_it.how: The model emits tables inline as markup which normalise_ocr_page flattens to pipe-rows inside the page text, so the content rides in new_text; pinned by the flatten test with a parking-rate table.
break_it.repro: normalise_ocr_page on a table fragment yields Dwelling house | 2 spaces rows.

break_it.scenario: A clean chapter gets needlessly routed through OCR, adding cost and cold-start latency to every cron run.
break_it.what_happens: Cron runtime and Modal spend balloon for no fidelity gain.
break_it.how: The trigger requires actual doubled-glyph runs in the raw text layer; clean layers (including legitimate doubles like Lloyd/III) never fire, pinned by tests.
break_it.repro: text_layer_garbled on clean pages returns False.

break_it.scenario: An unauthorised caller uses the public endpoint to run free GPU OCR.
break_it.what_happens: Modal spend on someone else's documents.
break_it.how: Shared-secret header checked in-function against the Modal secret; smoke test confirmed 401 without the token. Residual: rotate MODAL_OCR_TOKEN if leaked (it lives in .env and Railway env).

post_merge.db_reset: Not required - no schema or data changes.
post_merge.secrets: MODAL_OCR_TOKEN added to root .env and Modal secret ocr-service-token; must also be set with MODAL_OCR_URL on Railway dcp-extract and dcp-extract-all services (dashboard env, not git).
post_merge.other_repo: None. Modal deploy source is scripts/modal_ocr_service.py in this repo; redeploy with modal deploy after edits.
post_merge.manual_verify: Yes - after Railway env is set: re-run extraction for the 7 held chapters; garbled ones print OCR lines and enqueue clean rows; with the endpoint stopped the same run degrades to text-layer rows flagged failed.
